title: How to turn your employee handbook into short training videos
summary: Turn your employee handbook into short training videos: which policies to film, how to split them, translation, acknowledgement, and policy updates.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


- Make a video only where the handbook asks an employee to act or decide, one policy or decision per video, mostly under three minutes.
- Keep legal wording and benefit plan documents as text. The handbook stays the binding version.
- Build each video from the handbook section or orientation deck you already have, and have the policy owner approve the script.
- Caption everything and translate what your workforce needs. Record acknowledgement in your HRIS or LMS, not the video.
- When a policy changes, edit the affected script line and re-export. Embedded videos update in place.
- Clueso turns a handbook PDF, Word doc, or slide deck into a narrated video and written guide on every plan, including Free.


Your employee handbook already does its legal job. It states every policy in full, it carries an acknowledgement page, and the signed copy in your HRIS shows what each person was given. What it doesn't do is teach a new hire how to report a concern or book leave in the week they first need to.


So HR teams cut the handbook into short videos, and the first batch is the manageable part. The harder part comes later, when legal rewrites the code of conduct and you have to find every video that still teaches the old version.


This guide covers both: which sections deserve a video, how to produce them from documents you already have, how to handle translation and acknowledgement, and what to do when a policy changes. It ends with how[Clueso turns a handbook PDF into a narrated video](https://www.clueso.io/tools/pdf-to-video-converter) . If you're comparing tools instead, our roundup of[AI video tools for compliance training](https://www.clueso.io/blog/best-ai-video-tools-for-compliance-training) covers the options.


## Which parts of an employee handbook should become training videos?


Employee handbook training videos are short narrated videos, each covering one policy or one decision from your handbook, that show employees what to do and when. They sit alongside the handbook rather than replacing it. Most run one to three minutes, and each points back to the section it teaches.


The test is whether an employee has to act on the section. Reporting harassment and accepting a gift from a supplier both come down to a moment where someone has to choose what to do, and a two-minute video with a worked example teaches that moment better than a paragraph of policy language.


Sections that exist to be on record should stay as text, because a narrated summary of a legal text is a second version that can drift out of sync with the first. Benefits are the clearest case. US federal rules require a summary plan description[written "in a manner calculated to be understood by the average plan participant"](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/2520.102-2) , and that document is what the plan is held to, whatever a video says.

## How do you split a handbook into short videos?


Split by decision, not by chapter. A chapter called "Workplace conduct" can hold half a dozen separate rules. Put them in one 12-minute video and the person trying to find out who to call about a manager's comment scrubs through conflicts of interest first.


One decision per video keeps each one short. Across 26,610 videos customers exported from Clueso in the year to October 21, 2026, the median ran 91 seconds, and our guide on[how long a training video should be](https://www.clueso.io/blog/how-long-should-a-training-video-be) recommends keeping each policy module under six minutes. At about 130 words a minute of narration, a two-minute video holds roughly 260 words, less than a page of most handbooks.


Before you make anything, build a map: a sheet with every handbook section, the video that teaches it, and the policy's effective date. It won't help with the first batch, but it's the first thing you'll open when a policy changes.


1. Mark every section that asks an employee to act or decide.
2. Split each one into a video per decision, and check its length against the word count.
3. Rank the list by how often HR answers questions about each policy, and start at the top.
4. Title each video for the question an employee would ask, such as "How do I report a concern?" rather than "Section 4.2".
5. Add each video to the map, and put the policy's effective date on its closing card too.


## How do you turn the handbook or onboarding slides into a narrated video?


Work from one section of the handbook, not the whole PDF. Two pages about the gifts policy leave room for a worked example, which a script built from all 40 pages won't have space for. Tell the tool or the scriptwriter who's watching and how long the video should run.


Build the script around a situation. "A supplier has offered you tickets to a game" teaches a gifts policy faster than reading the dollar threshold aloud. Keep the facts identical to the handbook, such as thresholds, deadlines, and the name of the reporting channel, because employees will repeat whatever the video told them.


Then the policy owner reviews the script. That's usually HR, with legal for anything disciplinary, reading it against the handbook before the video goes out and again after any translation. If a video quotes the wrong notice period, employees will act on the video.


### What about new hire orientation slides?


Orientation decks convert well because they're already split into slides, often with speaker notes. A[slide deck to video](https://www.clueso.io/features/ppt-video) tool narrates each slide from its notes or content, so the deck HR presents to every cohort becomes a video new hires watch before day one, and the live session goes to questions. Our guide to[employee onboarding videos](https://www.clueso.io/blog/employee-onboarding-videos-with-examples) covers which orientation videos to make first.


## How do you handle captions and translation for a multilingual workforce?


Caption every policy video. Employees often watch training on a phone without headphones, and captions make the video usable for anyone who is deaf or hard of hearing. Export the caption file as SRT or VTT so it travels with the video into your LMS.


Translation is a bigger decision, and sometimes the law makes it for you. Foreign-born workers made up 19.1% of the US civilian labor force in 2025, according to the[Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/forbrn.nr0.htm) . New York's[Labor Law 201-g](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/LAB/201-G) requires the sexual harassment policy and training information in English and in each employee's primary language, at hiring and at every annual training. For benefits, the federal SPD rule requires a notice offering help in a shared non-English language once enough participants read only that language. For plans with 100 or more participants, that's 500 people or 10%, whichever is lower.


Translate the approved script, not the source PDF, so every language says what the policy owner signed off. Have a fluent reader check terms with legal weight, such as leave types and reporting channels. A video that shows your HR system in English still shows English screens after the voiceover is dubbed, so record the localized interface or let the narration carry the meaning.


## How do you record that employees watched and acknowledged a policy?


A video isn't an acknowledgement. The record that someone received and agreed to a policy belongs where your handbook sign-offs already live, usually the HRIS or the LMS. The video makes that signature an informed one.


If you train through an LMS, export each video as a SCORM package so completion lands in the same report as everything else.[SCORM export](https://www.clueso.io/features/scorm-export) is on Clueso's Enterprise plan and reports completion and quiz scores to the LMS. Without an LMS, embed the video inside the HRIS acknowledgement task, so employees watch and sign in one place. Our guide to[adding training videos to an LMS](https://www.clueso.io/blog/add-training-videos-to-lms) covers the options.


Short videos don't satisfy mandated harassment training on their own. California requires employers with five or more employees to give nonsupervisory staff one hour and supervisors two hours of harassment prevention training every two years, according to its[Civil Rights Department](https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/2025/12/17/civil-rights-department-reminds-employers-and-employees-to-complete-sexual-harassment-prevention-training/) , and New York requires interactive training every year. A two-minute video on the reporting route supports that training without replacing it.


Keep the approval trail in your own systems as well. Clueso doesn't have a formal approval workflow or a customer-facing audit log, so store the policy owner's sign-off for each script wherever you keep policy approvals today.


## What do you do when a policy changes, like a new code of conduct?


This is where handbook video libraries go stale. The code of conduct gets a new hotline number or a lower gift threshold, the PDF is updated in a day, and the videos keep teaching the old rule because nobody knows which ones mention it.


Your map fixes that. When legal sends the redline, look up each changed section and you have the list of videos to touch, most of them needing a sentence or two changed.


Then edit the videos instead of remaking them. In a video built from a script with an[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) , a changed policy line is a text change: rewrite the sentence, regenerate the voiceover for that line, fix any on-screen text that shows the old figure, and re-export. If the video is[embedded on your intranet or HRIS](https://www.clueso.io/features/embed-videos-anywhere) , the embed code stays the same and serves the new version everywhere. A SCORM course on Clueso Enterprise takes one Publish update click and keeps each learner's completion history.


Update the effective date on the closing card and in your map, and decide whether the change needs a fresh acknowledgement. A new reporting route probably does, and a corrected typo doesn't. Rebuild from scratch only when the process has new steps, since patching a structure that no longer exists takes longer than starting again. Our guide to[updating part of a training video without re-recording](https://www.clueso.io/blog/update-training-video-without-re-recording) covers each kind of change.


## How do you make open enrollment and benefits videos employees will actually watch?


Make one video per decision an employee faces in the window: choosing a medical plan, whether to fund an HSA or FSA, adding a dependent, and enrolling in your benefits system. Keep each under two minutes and publish them a week or two before the window opens, while people still have time to compare.


Keep every number that changes yearly, such as premiums, contribution limits, and enrollment dates, in editable script lines and on-screen text, so next year's update is a text edit. Close each video by pointing to the summary plan description as the official terms.

## Frequently asked questions


### What's the best HR training video software for a small HR team?


Look for a tool that starts from documents you already have and lets someone without editing skills update a video when a policy changes. Our[AI video tools for compliance training](https://www.clueso.io/blog/best-ai-video-tools-for-compliance-training) roundup compares the options. Clueso converts PDFs, Word docs, and decks into narrated videos on every plan, and Business covers two editors for $120 a month billed yearly.


### How do I turn a policy document into a training video with AI?


Split the document into one policy per video, upload each section to a document to video tool, and have the policy owner review the script before export. Clueso's[PDF to video converter](https://www.clueso.io/tools/pdf-to-video-converter) drafts the script, adds an AI voiceover and motion graphics, and writes a matching guide, on every plan.


### We updated our code of conduct. How do we update the training video without starting over?


Find the videos covering the changed sections, edit the affected script lines, regenerate the voiceover for those lines, and re-export. In Clueso, an embedded video keeps its embed code and shows the new version wherever it's posted, and an Enterprise SCORM course updates in the LMS with one Publish update click.


### Can a training video replace the signed handbook acknowledgement?


No. Keep the acknowledgement in your HRIS or LMS and place the video inside that task so the signature is informed. If your LMS tracks training, Clueso's SCORM export on Enterprise reports completion and quiz scores to it. Our[compliance training videos](https://www.clueso.io/use-cases/compliance-training-videos) page covers policy training more broadly.


Before you open any tool, pull last quarter's HR inbox and count which handbook policy people asked about most. Make that your first video, keep it under two minutes, and add its row to the map with today's effective date. The next time someone asks, send the link instead of the paragraph.
